 :J U D G M E N T:

This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 04.12.2021.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 04.12.2021 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding by riding the Honda Dio bearing No. KA.53.EL.6216 on Varthur main road, when he reached near Mukesh Kumar Nursery, at that time the driver of the Cab bearing Reg.No. KA.03.AF.5145 driven the vehicle with high speed in a rash or negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner from opposite direction and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Columbia Asia hospital,
later he was admitted to Manipal hospital, wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.

Petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment, food, transport and other charges.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner was aged about 58 years, working as a security supervisor at Adarsha Groups, Kannahalli, Bangalore and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month.
Due to injuries sustained in the accident, he is not able to continue his work and has sustained loss of income.
The Whitefield police have registered the case in Cr.No.85/2021 against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.

The 1st respondent being the R.C.
owner and the 2 nd respondent being insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, this petition.
3. After service of notice, both the respondents have appeared through their respective counsels but 1st respondent has not filed written statement.

4. The written statement averments of the 2nd respondent are hereunder:
This respondent has denied the issuance of policy in respect of Car bearing No.
KA.03.AF.5145 and the liability of this respondent is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, the owner of the offending Car has Manjunath.V vs Ramachandra M.R on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25679942/
2 entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license and the vehicle was also not having valid FC and permit as on the date of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act and Sec.158(b) of M.V. Act.
Further contended that, complaint was lodged after the lapse of 2 days from the cause of accident by falsely implicating the offending Car in the alleged accident.
Further it has also contended that, the petitioner was riding the vehicle without having valid driving license.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also contended that, the claim petition is barred by limitation and hence liable to be dismissed.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
:ISSUES:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in accident occurred on 04.12.2021 at 8.30 p.m. near Mukesh Kumar Nursery, due to rash and negligent driving of Cab bearing registration No. KA.03.AF.5145 by its driver as contended in the petition ?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that, he is entitled for the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3.
What order
or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.
P.W.1 was cross-examined from the side of respondent No.2.
Further the petitioner has examined the billing supervisor at Manipal hospital as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P16.

MRO of Manipal hospital is examined as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P17 to Ex.P20 and also examined the billing supervisor at Manipal hospital as PW.4 and through him got marked the documents at Ex.P21 to Ex.P23.
The evidence of PW.2 was not challenged.
PW.3 & PW.4 were cross examined from the side of 2nd respondent.
In spite of sufficient opportunity respondents have not lead any evidence.
7. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

8. The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- In the Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :- As per the final order, for the following:

sentences.text: ISSUE No.1:-

Before going to discuss issue No.1 it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009)
13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
Therefore it is crystal clear that the petitioner has to prove his case based on the principle of preponderance of probabilities.
10. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
In order to substantiate the oral evidence, P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.85/2021.
Ex . P.2
is the true copy of complaint.
Ex . P.3
is the true copy of spot mahazar.
Ex . P.4
is the true copy of spot sketch.
Ex.P.5 is the true copy of MVA report.
Ex.P.6 is the true copy of wound certificate.
Ex . P.7 & 8 are the true copies of notice and reply U/Sec.133.
Ex . P.9
is the true copy of bond.
Ex.P.10 is the true copy of MLC intimation and Ex.P.11 is the true copy of charge sheet.

11. At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
12. According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.

According to the respondent No.2, owner of the offending Car has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license and the vehicle was also not having valid FC and permit as on the date of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.
Further contended that, complaint was lodged after the lapse of 2 days from the cause of accident by falsely implicating the offending Car in the alleged accident.

Further it has also contended that, the petitioner was riding the vehicle without having valid driving license and also contended that, the claim petition is barred by limitation and hence liable to be dismissed.
In order to substantiate the same, respondent No.2 has neither examined any witness nor produced documents.
13. Further, to prove the alleged negligence on the part of petitioner, the Insurance Company has cross- examined the petitioner/P.W.1 in detail.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of petitioner.
14. Further, the contention of respondent No.2 is that, complaint has been lodged after 2 days of the accident.
On perusal of Ex.P.2, it reveals that, the complainant has explained the delay for filing complaint.
In other words the complainant has stated that, on account of taking treatment, there is a delay in lodging complaint.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Manjunath.V vs Ramachandra M.R on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25679942/

sentences.text:
Court reported in 2011 (4) SCC 693, between Ravi Vs. Badrinarayana and Others, wherein it is held that:
"It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case. Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot except a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim".
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with the closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The principles reiterated in the above decision squarely applicable to the facts of the case.
The ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the instant case.
15. In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the driver of Car bearing Reg.No. KA.03.AF.5145.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.2, complaint was lodged before Whitefield traffic Police Station.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.11, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.11 after completing investigation.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.6, it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.11 i.e.,
charge sheet
, it reveals that, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No. KA.03.AF.5145 has arrayed as accused.

16. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the petitioner was proceeding by riding the Honda Dio bearing No. KA.53.EL.6216 on Varthur main road, when he reached near Mukesh Kumar Nursery, at that time the driver of the Cab bearing Reg.No. KA.03.AF.5145 driven the vehicle with high speed in a rash or negligent manner,
endangering to human life and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner from opposite direction and caused the accident.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that driver of the offending Cab bearing Reg.No. KA.03.AF.5145 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:- Already this Tribunal has observed that, the accident was caused due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of offending Cab bearing Reg.No. KA.03.AF.5145.
It is needless to mention that, 1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The 2 nd respondent is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

18. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-

5
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has sustained Sub Arachniod haemorrhage-right parietal region, Subgleal hematoma right frontal region and other injuries.
P.W.1 has stated that, immediately after the accident, he was rushed to Columbia Asia hospital and thereafter he was shifted to Manipal hospital, wherein he has taken treatment.
In support of his evidence, petitioner has examined the billing supervisor at Manipal hospital as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P16.

MRO of Manipal hospital is examined as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P17 to Ex.P20 and also the billing supervisor at Manipal hospital as PW.4 and through him got marked the documents at Ex.P21 to Ex.P23.
On perusal of Ex.P.16 it reveals that, the petitioner was treated at Manipal Hospital as an inpatient from 05.12.2021 to 09.12.2021.

On perusal of Ex.P18, it reveals that the petitioner has sustained multiple contused abrasions present over face, fore head, head injury with subtrihantic hemorrhage right parietal region and other injuries.
It is relevant to mention that,
respondent
No.2 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
19 . The petitioner has stated that, after the accident, he is unable to do any work and he is suffering from permanent disability and lost his future.
It is relevant to note that, the 2nd respondent has denied the disability sustained to petitioner.
In order to prove the disability, the petitioner has not examined the medical witness.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.
20. Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced 4 medical bills marked as Ex.P.14 for Rs.1,32,499/-.
In addition to the evidence of PW.1 the petitioner examined the billing supervisor as PW.2.
In his affidavit he has stated that, the petitioner was admitted and treated in their hospital.
The inpatient bill amount was Rs.1,25,799/- and insurance company has paid Rs.56,800/- and remaining amount of Rs.68,958/- was paid by the petitioner.
He has produced duplicate copy of the bill which has been marked as Ex.P16.
It is relevant to note that the evidence of PW.2 is remained unchallenged.
On careful perusal of Ex.P16, it reveals that the total bill amount is Rs.1,25,799/-.
Out of which on 05.12.2021 Rs.5,000/- was paid in cash, on 09.12.2021 a sum of Rs.63,958/- was paid in cash.
Further on 24.05.2022 a sum of Rs.51,157/- paid through cheque and on the same day itself Rs.5,684/- has been transferred through bank.
Therefore it appears to this tribunal that the entire bill amount has not been paid by the insurance company.
As stated by PW.2, the insurance company paid only Rs.56,841/- and remaining amount of Rs.68,958/- was paid by the petitioner.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.68,958/- towards medical expenses.
21. Pain and suffering:-
According to the petitioner, he has suffered due to multiple contused abrasions present over face, fore head, head injury with subtrihantic hemorrhage right parietal region and other injuries.
Further, P.W.1 has stated that, due to injuries sustianed in the accident, he is unable to do any work and carry out his day to day activities.
As per medical records it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner has taken treatment at Manipal hospital.
In the instant case, the petitioner has not produced discharge summary.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

6 22. Loss of income during the laidup period:-
The petitioner has not produced discharge summary and he has not stated about the treatment taken as an inpatient.
However, the petitioner has not produced documents to show that, how many days he has taken bed rest.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
23. Food, Nourishment, Atttendant and Transportation charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has not produced discharge summary.
Hence, he is not entitled for compensation under the head of Food, Nourishment, Atttendant and transportation charges.
24. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 58 years at the time of accident.
The petitioner has not sustained any disability and physical deformity due to accidental injuries.
Therefore, he is not entitled for compensation under this head.

25. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Amount  1.Towards loss of Future income.
- Nil -  2. Towards Medical Expenses.
3. Towards Pain & Suffering.

4. Loss of income during the  laidup - Nil -  period  5. Food, Nourishment Atttendant - Nil -  and transportation charges  6. Loss of future amenities and - Nil -  happiness.
 7.
Towards future medical - Nil -  expenses.

Total. Rs.93,958/-
Hence, petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.93,958/-.
26. Regarding liability and interest.
Manjunath.V vs Ramachandra M.R on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25679942/
7 Driving License:-
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Moreover at the time of issuing reply to the notice issued U/Sec.133 of MV Act, there is clear mentioning of driving license number.
Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:-
In the written statement the respondent No.2 has denied the issuance of policy with respect to Car bearing No. KA.03.AF.5145.
Further contended that, the vehicle has no permit.
Again it is worth to take Ex.P8.
As per Ex.P8 the owner of the offending vehicle has clearly mentioned the pemit number and its validity.
Further he has mentioned the policy number also.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioner.

27. In view of the decision reported in MFA NO:
30131-2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another,
rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Issue No.4 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.
28. ISSUE No.3:-
In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.

Petitioner is awarded global  compensation of Rs.93,958/- (Rupees Ninety three thousand nine hundred and fifty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.

:APPORTIONMENT:
Scheme of investment is dispensed with as amount awarded is too meager.
